ableton_user_goal: Switch between linear arrangement and clip-launching grid
live_behavior: Press Tab to toggle Arrangement and Session View.
ardour_native_capability: Editor and Cue Grid are separate modes with menu actions and customizable shortcuts.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind Tab to a reversible Editor/Cue toggle; label the profile surfaces Arrangement and Session while retaining Ardour names in help.
acceptance_criterion: From either workspace, one Tab press opens the other and preserves selection and transport.
risk_note: Must not interfere with Tab-based focus navigation in text fields or dialogs.

ableton_user_goal: Switch the lower panel between clip editing and devices
live_behavior: Press Shift+Tab or F12 to switch Clip and Device View.
ardour_native_capability: The bottom pane can show MIDI/audio clip editing or generic plugin UI, but its switching model differs.
proposed_migration_behavior: Provide Shift+Tab as a deterministic Clip/Devices toggle and remember the last subview per workspace.
acceptance_criterion: Shift+Tab always switches between selected clip content and selected track processors without opening a modal.
risk_note: Requires a stable bottom-pane mode API and focus rules.

ableton_user_goal: Open, search and close one unified content browser
live_behavior: Use the left Browser for instruments, effects, plug-ins, clips, samples and places; Ctrl/Cmd+F searches.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour divides content among Editor/Cue lists, Clips, Sources, Regions, Favorite Plugins and Plugin Selector.
proposed_migration_behavior: Present a unified left browser facade with categories backed by existing Ardour sources; Ctrl/Cmd+F focuses its search.
acceptance_criterion: One search locates a plug-in, preset or clip and Enter/drag inserts it in the valid target.
risk_note: Core migration blocker: fragmented discovery currently breaks Live browser muscle memory.

ableton_user_goal: Navigate primary work areas entirely from the keyboard
live_behavior: Use focus shortcuts and predictable Tab navigation among Control Bar, Session, Arrangement, Clip, Device and Browser.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has contextual keybindings but no Live-equivalent focus map across these exact surfaces.
proposed_migration_behavior: Add a workspace focus model with Alt/Option+number targets and visible focus indication.
acceptance_criterion: A keyboard-only user can focus Browser, timeline/grid, lower pane and transport and operate the focused control.
risk_note: Must coexist with accessibility APIs and platform menu conventions.

ableton_user_goal: Use a second display for another production view
live_behavior: Toggle Live's second window and place Arrangement/Session or detail views there.
ardour_native_capability: Editor, Mixer, Recorder and Cue Grid can be detached and shown simultaneously.
proposed_migration_behavior: Map the Live shortcut to a saved two-window workspace profile; retain Ardour's detachable-window model.
acceptance_criterion: The shortcut opens the configured secondary view on the previous display and a second press hides it.
risk_note: Window-manager behavior varies by platform.

ableton_user_goal: Have the detail editor follow the current selection
live_behavior: Clip View follows the selected audio or MIDI clip; Device View follows the selected track.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour's bottom pane and processor views are selection-aware but use different presentation and persistence rules.
proposed_migration_behavior: Normalize selection-follow behavior and add a pin control for users who do not want launched clips to steal focus.
acceptance_criterion: Selecting an audio region, MIDI region or track shows the expected editor or processor view without surprising focus changes.
risk_note: Cue launching and selection must be independently configurable.

ableton_user_goal: Start a new production session quickly
live_behavior: Create a new Live Set with familiar default tracks and routing.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour creates sessions through its New Session dialog and supports factory/user templates.
proposed_migration_behavior: Make a Beat Production template the default profile choice with audio, MIDI, two effect buses and Master.
acceptance_criterion: A new session opens with the documented tracks, musical time, grid, buses and monitoring in under three user actions.
risk_note: Do not silently replace the user's chosen audio backend or I/O device.

ableton_user_goal: Open, save and save a version under another name
live_behavior: Use Ctrl/Cmd+O, Ctrl/Cmd+S and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour provides New, Open, Save, Save As and snapshot/version operations.
proposed_migration_behavior: Use Live-compatible file shortcuts while teaching Ardour snapshots as an additional versioning feature.
acceptance_criterion: Open, Save and Save As use expected shortcuts and never overwrite an unrelated session.
risk_note: Clarify Session versus snapshot terminology during onboarding.

ableton_user_goal: Reuse a trusted production setup
live_behavior: Save and reuse a default Set or track/device configuration.
ardour_native_capability: Session templates store tracks, buses, plugins and I/O; track templates store whole track state.
proposed_migration_behavior: Ship production templates and expose Save as Template in the migration tour and command search.
acceptance_criterion: A user can save a configured session as a template and create an equivalent new session from it.
risk_note: Templates containing third-party plugins need missing-plugin handling.

ableton_user_goal: Import audio or MIDI by dragging it into the project
live_behavior: Drag browser or desktop files to Session/Arrangement tracks; Live creates or populates tracks as appropriate.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour imports audio/MIDI through the dialog or drag/drop to tracks, Region List or empty editor space.
proposed_migration_behavior: Preserve drag/drop insertion and teach where clips, regions and new tracks are created; add browser insertion affordances.
acceptance_criterion: Dragging WAV or MIDI from the browser to an empty timeline area creates a usable track at the drop position.
risk_note: Channel mapping and copy-versus-link choices should remain explicit but not interrupt common cases.

ableton_user_goal: Create an audio track
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+T inserts an audio track.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour can add audio tracks through Add Track/Bus/VCA and a keybinding.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind Ctrl/Cmd+T directly to add one stereo audio track after the selection; expose alternate configurations in a follow-up dialog/action.
acceptance_criterion: Shortcut creates one stereo audio track after the selected track and focuses its name.
risk_note: Ardour's general add dialog may require a small Lua action for one-step behavior.

ableton_user_goal: Create a MIDI track
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+T inserts a MIDI track.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour can add MIDI tracks and choose an instrument during creation.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind the Live shortcut to create one MIDI track, using the profile's default preview instrument or no instrument by preference.
acceptance_criterion: Shortcut creates one MIDI track and the track can immediately record or accept a MIDI region.
risk_note: Never require a proprietary instrument; default must be replaceable.

ableton_user_goal: Create a return/effect channel
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+T inserts a Return Track.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour uses audio buses with aux sends for shared effects.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind the shortcut to create a stereo effect bus, add aux sends from selected tracks and name it sequentially A, B, C.
acceptance_criterion: Shortcut creates a stereo bus routed to Master and makes a usable send available from selected tracks.
risk_note: A return is a workflow convention over Ardour's more general routing model.

ableton_user_goal: Rename tracks quickly in sequence
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+R renames; Tab advances to the next track.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour supports track naming and keyboard customization but sequencing behavior differs.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind rename and implement Tab/Shift+Tab traversal while the inline name editor is active.
acceptance_criterion: Rename begins inline and Tab commits and advances without triggering workspace switching.
risk_note: Requires context-sensitive Tab behavior.

ableton_user_goal: Duplicate a complete track
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+D duplicates selected tracks and their devices/clips.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour can create templates/copies, but exact one-step duplication semantics are not surfaced like Live.
proposed_migration_behavior: Add a Lua action that duplicates route configuration and optionally playlist content with an explicit default.
acceptance_criterion: The shortcut creates one adjacent track with matching routing/processors and the documented playlist-copy policy.
risk_note: Must define shared versus independent playlists to avoid destructive surprises.

ableton_user_goal: Group and ungroup tracks
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+G creates a Group Track; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G removes it.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has route groups, subgroup buses and VCAs, which separate control grouping from signal grouping.
proposed_migration_behavior: Default to a visual route group; offer Create Subgroup Bus as a distinct command in the contextual menu.
acceptance_criterion: Group shortcut creates a collapsible logical group without silently changing routing; explicit subgrouping changes routing.
risk_note: Live Group Track combines concepts that Ardour intentionally separates.

ableton_user_goal: Arm selected tracks
live_behavior: Press C in Live 12 to arm selected tracks.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has per-track record enable and commands that can be rebound.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind C in the timeline/grid context to toggle record enable on selected recordable tracks.
acceptance_criterion: C toggles arm for selected audio/MIDI tracks and ignores buses.
risk_note: C must retain text-entry behavior in naming/search fields.

ableton_user_goal: Solo selected tracks
live_behavior: Press S to solo selected tracks.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has solo controls and selection-aware actions, but S is commonly used for Split in Ardour defaults.
proposed_migration_behavior: In the Live profile, S means Solo when track headers are focused; Ctrl/Cmd+E performs Split.
acceptance_criterion: S toggles solo for selected tracks and never splits a region in the Live profile.
risk_note: High-visibility collision with Ardour documentation; profile badge and shortcut help are essential.

ableton_user_goal: Deactivate a selected track or clip
live_behavior: Press 0 to deactivate selected tracks, clips, notes or devices.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has mute, region mute and processor bypass, but not one uniform deactivate model.
proposed_migration_behavior: Map 0 contextually: track mute, region mute, MIDI-note mute where available, processor bypass; document the semantic differences.
acceptance_criterion: 0 toggles the reversible inactive state appropriate to the focused object and provides visible feedback.
risk_note: Do not conflate audio mute with disabling DSP load.

ableton_user_goal: Reorder and resize tracks directly
live_behavior: Drag track headers; use modifier+arrow for keyboard reordering; resize lanes.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour supports track ordering, height adjustment and track lists.
proposed_migration_behavior: Keep native drag behavior; add Live-compatible keyboard reorder and consistent fold/height commands.
acceptance_criterion: Selected tracks can be reordered and resized without losing their selection or group membership.
risk_note: Track-header side should not change ordering semantics.

ableton_user_goal: Route tracks and use sends without leaving the main workflow
live_behavior: Live exposes I/O and Sends in Session/Arrangement and uses Return Tracks.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour supports arbitrary I/O, buses, aux sends and routing grids with greater flexibility.
proposed_migration_behavior: Provide simplified In/Out and Sends panels that reveal Ardour's routing grid through an Advanced action.
acceptance_criterion: A user can route a track to Master, choose an input and send to A Reverb without opening the full routing grid.
risk_note: Simplification must not hide or rewrite existing complex routes.

ableton_user_goal: Mix from Arrangement without changing to a separate mixer
live_behavior: Live can show volume, pan, sends, I/O and meters beside Arrangement tracks.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour's Editor can show one channel strip; full mixing is primarily in the Mixer window.
proposed_migration_behavior: Add a compact right-side track-control column with configurable volume/pan/sends/meter visibility.
acceptance_criterion: Arrangement displays useful controls for every visible track and updates the same underlying mixer state.
risk_note: Major visual/topological migration blocker; should be a generic side preference.

ableton_user_goal: Split a clip at the insertion point
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+E splits the selected clip or time selection.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour Split/Separate cuts selected regions at the edit point.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind Ctrl/Cmd+E to Split using a predictable playhead/selection edit-point policy.
acceptance_criterion: With one selected region, the shortcut produces two non-destructive regions at the visible insertion marker.
risk_note: Ardour edit-point modes can surprise Live users; profile should default to playhead/selection.

ableton_user_goal: Trim a clip by dragging its edges
live_behavior: Drag clip boundaries with snapping; fades remain editable.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour regions support non-destructive drag trimming with Snap settings.
proposed_migration_behavior: Use native trimming and Live-like cursor/selection feedback; teach slip editing as an Ardour extension.
acceptance_criterion: Dragging either edge changes only the region boundary, obeys grid state and remains undoable.
risk_note: Cursor styling belongs to theme/UI polish rather than behavior.

ableton_user_goal: Duplicate clips or a time selection
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+D duplicates the focused material immediately after itself.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour Duplicate and Multi-Duplicate append selected regions; range operations also exist.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind Ctrl/Cmd+D contextually to region or range duplication and preserve the selection on the new copy.
acceptance_criterion: The shortcut duplicates selected material once to the expected next grid-aligned location.
risk_note: Track duplication must use a different focus context or explicit command.

ableton_user_goal: Consolidate an edited span into one clip
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+J consolidates the time selection.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour Consolidate Range joins material per track; Bounce creates new source files with optional processing.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind Ctrl/Cmd+J to Consolidate Range and expose Bounce with Processing as a separate command.
acceptance_criterion: A selected time span on one track becomes one region with expected silence and boundaries.
risk_note: Clarify whether processing is printed; default consolidation should not print the mixer chain.

ableton_user_goal: Set or toggle a loop around the selection
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+L toggles the Arrangement loop based on the current selection.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour can set Loop Range from regions/ranges and toggle loop playback.
proposed_migration_behavior: Create one Lua action that sets the loop from selection when needed and toggles loop playback otherwise.
acceptance_criterion: Shortcut creates a loop from selected time/regions and starts or disables loop mode predictably.
risk_note: Define behavior when there is no selection and an existing loop range exists.

ableton_user_goal: Nudge material by grid or a smaller increment
live_behavior: Use arrow/modifier operations to move clips and selections precisely.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour provides nudge earlier/later and grid-relative movement actions.
proposed_migration_behavior: Map Live-style modifiers to Ardour nudge actions and display the active nudge/grid amount in the status bar.
acceptance_criterion: Nudging moves selected regions by the displayed amount, remains undoable and preserves track placement.
risk_note: Platform modifier conventions need separate profiles.

ableton_user_goal: Zoom into a selection and return to the previous zoom
live_behavior: Press Z to zoom to selection and X to return.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour offers zoom controls and zoom-to-selection/fit operations, but history semantics differ.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind Z to zoom selection and add a small Lua-managed previous-zoom stack for X if no native action matches.
acceptance_criterion: Repeated Z operations can be unwound in order with X without moving the playhead or selection.
risk_note: Zoom history must be isolated per editor window.

ableton_user_goal: Show and edit automation lanes
live_behavior: Press A for Automation Mode; choose a parameter and draw breakpoints.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour exposes automation lanes for tracks and processors and supports drawing curves.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind A to show/hide automation for the selected track and preserve native parameter selection.
acceptance_criterion: A toggles automation visibility and a selected parameter can be edited with breakpoints in the timeline.
risk_note: Live's global mode and Ardour's lane-centric model differ; do not hide automation state.

ableton_user_goal: Record parameter movements as automation
live_behavior: Use Automation Arm and record movements into Arrangement.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour supports Manual, Play, Write, Touch and Latch automation states.
proposed_migration_behavior: Provide a Live-like Automation Arm macro that safely places selected controls in Touch, with explicit Write/Latch choices.
acceptance_criterion: When armed, moving an eligible parameter while rolling writes automation; stopping returns to a safe state.
risk_note: Never silently put multiple lanes into destructive Write mode.

ableton_user_goal: Record multiple takes and build a comp
live_behavior: Show Take Lanes, audition lanes and copy selected passages to the main lane.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour uses playlists and/or stacked layers for takes; comp construction is less lane-oriented.
proposed_migration_behavior: Create a Comping workspace and Lua helpers over playlists; clearer lane presentation in an Ardour source change if testing confirms the need.
acceptance_criterion: A vocalist can record three takes, audition them and assemble a composite without manually creating extra tracks.
risk_note: Terminology and visual feedback are substantial differences despite comparable underlying capability.

ableton_user_goal: Warp audio elastically to project tempo with local timing edits
live_behavior: Enable Warp, set Warp Markers and choose a mode; clips follow tempo without changing pitch.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour can stretch regions and tempo-sync Cue clips, but does not provide Live-equivalent per-clip Warp Marker editing.
proposed_migration_behavior: Present Cue tempo-sync and region stretch honestly; mark local Warp Marker editing as a non-equivalent feature gap.
acceptance_criterion: A migration guide demonstrates supported whole-clip sync and explicitly states that arbitrary Live Warp Marker workflows do not map exactly.
risk_note: Do not market full Live-style warping until it exists and passes audio-quality tests.

ableton_user_goal: Create a MIDI clip/region at a chosen musical length
live_behavior: Double-click an empty MIDI track area or record into a clip slot.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour creates and records MIDI regions and can record MIDI clips into Cue slots.
proposed_migration_behavior: Add one-click Create MIDI Clip actions for timeline selection and empty Cue slots, using current grid/loop length.
acceptance_criterion: A user creates a one-bar MIDI region on the selected track without opening a general-purpose dialog.
risk_note: Default region length must be visible and changeable.

ableton_user_goal: Edit notes in a focused lower editor
live_behavior: Double-click a MIDI clip to open Clip View; draw, move and resize notes.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour 9 provides in-place, bottom-pane and separate pianoroll editing.
proposed_migration_behavior: Default double-click and Shift+Tab behavior to the bottom pianoroll while retaining separate-window editing as an option.
acceptance_criterion: Double-clicking a MIDI region opens it in the lower editor with notes editable and transport context preserved.
risk_note: Ardour 9.7 improvements should be the target baseline.

ableton_user_goal: Quantize notes with familiar shortcuts
live_behavior: Ctrl/Cmd+U quantizes; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+U opens quantize settings.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has quantization in MIDI Tools/pianoroll and customizable shortcuts.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind the Live shortcuts to apply current quantize and focus/open MIDI Tools settings.
acceptance_criterion: Quantize applies the visible settings to selected notes and can be undone.
risk_note: If no notes are selected, document whether the region or all notes are affected.

ableton_user_goal: Edit velocity, CC and note expression
live_behavior: Use Clip View lanes/panels for velocity, controllers and MPE.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour pianoroll automation lanes edit velocity and MIDI controllers; MPE parity is not assumed.
proposed_migration_behavior: Map velocity and CC workflows; list unsupported expression dimensions explicitly rather than hiding them.
acceptance_criterion: A user can display and edit velocity plus at least one MIDI CC lane in the lower editor.
risk_note: MPE and Live-specific MIDI tools require a separate capability audit.

ableton_user_goal: Edit notes from multiple clips together
live_behavior: Live supports multi-clip MIDI editing and contextual note views.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour documentation states note data is edited in one region at a time, though reference/ghost notes have improved.
proposed_migration_behavior: Use ghost/reference notes for context and document that cross-region note selection/editing is not equivalent.
acceptance_criterion: The guide shows reference notes and clearly identifies the boundary: edits apply to one active MIDI region.
risk_note: A future multi-region editing change should be evaluated separately from the initial profile.

ableton_user_goal: Search for and insert an instrument or effect
live_behavior: Search Browser, select a device and press Enter or drag it to a track/device chain.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour provides Plugin Selector search/tags, Favorite Plugins and drag/drop to Processor Boxes.
proposed_migration_behavior: Unify discovery in the left browser; until an Ardour source change exists, map Ctrl/Cmd+F to Plugin Selector when a processor target is focused.
acceptance_criterion: Typing a plugin name and pressing Enter inserts it on the selected track at the visible insertion point.
risk_note: Search target and insertion location must be unambiguous.

ableton_user_goal: Reorder or copy processors by dragging
live_behavior: Drag devices horizontally within or between device chains.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour Processor Boxes support drag/drop reordering and copying between tracks.
proposed_migration_behavior: Keep native behavior; present the chain horizontally in the Live workspace while preserving processor order and pre/post-fader meaning.
acceptance_criterion: Dragging a processor changes order or copies it to another track and the audio signal order matches the visual order.
risk_note: Horizontal presentation must still show the fader boundary and channel-count changes.

ableton_user_goal: Bypass the selected processor
live_behavior: Press 0 or click the device activator.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour processors expose enable/bypass controls and support selection.
proposed_migration_behavior: Map 0 contextually to processor bypass and style the state consistently with track/region deactivation.
acceptance_criterion: 0 toggles selected processors without deleting them and displays a strong inactive state.
risk_note: Some plugins have their own bypass; distinguish host bypass from plugin controls.

ableton_user_goal: Load a preset or quickly replace a device
live_behavior: Use presets and Hot-Swap to audition replacements in context.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour Plugin Selector/Favorites exposes presets and searchable alternatives but not the same Hot-Swap state machine.
proposed_migration_behavior: Provide preset browsing immediately; defer true next/previous replacement audition to a unified browser source change.
acceptance_criterion: A user can load a preset and replace a processor without disturbing unrelated chain elements.
risk_note: Preset formats and plugin state vary by plugin standard.

ableton_user_goal: Launch and stop an individual clip
live_behavior: Click the clip launch triangle or press Enter; clip starts according to quantization.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour trigger slots launch/stop individual audio or MIDI clips and support MIDI learn.
proposed_migration_behavior: Use native Cue behavior with Live-profile icons, Enter launch and 0 deactivate where contextually safe.
acceptance_criterion: A selected clip launches on the configured quantization boundary and can be stopped independently.
risk_note: Selection-on-launch should be configurable to avoid changing the lower editor unexpectedly.

ableton_user_goal: Launch a whole scene/cue
live_behavior: Use the rightmost Scene Launch button to trigger one row.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour cues are rows with buttons A–P that launch all non-isolated slots.
proposed_migration_behavior: Present cues as Scenes in the alias layer and bind Enter to the selected cue button.
acceptance_criterion: Launching a cue starts all intended slots together and respects slot isolation and quantization.
risk_note: Docs should teach that Ardour's canonical term remains Cue.

ableton_user_goal: Record audio or MIDI directly into an empty clip slot
live_behavior: Arm Session recording and record a new clip with fixed length or until stopped.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour 9 can record audio/MIDI directly into Cue trigger slots and play back after quantization.
proposed_migration_behavior: Map the Live recording shortcut and make fixed-length recording visible near the selected slot.
acceptance_criterion: A user records a four-bar clip into an empty slot and it begins playback at the expected boundary.
risk_note: Input monitoring and global record state must remain obvious.

ableton_user_goal: Configure launch quantization and follow actions
live_behavior: Choose global/clip quantization, launch mode and follow actions such as Next, Again or random.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour trigger slots support launch styles, quantization, legato, follow actions and probability.
proposed_migration_behavior: Use native controls with terminology crosswalk and sensible one-bar defaults.
acceptance_criterion: A clip can launch on the next bar, repeat twice and then advance to another slot.
risk_note: Avoid changing Ardour defaults globally outside the profile/session template.

ableton_user_goal: Capture an improvised Session performance into a linear arrangement
live_behavior: Arrangement Record logs launched clips, automation, tempo and scene changes to the Arrangement.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour can combine Cue playback with timeline cue markers, but does not provide equivalent performance-to-regions capture semantics.
proposed_migration_behavior: Specify a generic Capture Cue Performance feature: log cue/slot launches to editable timeline events, then optionally render/commit regions.
acceptance_criterion: Recording a two-minute cue performance yields an editable, repeatable timeline representation matching what was heard.
risk_note: Largest functional migration gap after per-clip Warp Markers; requires explicit data model decisions.

ableton_user_goal: Export the master mix
live_behavior: Use Export Audio/Video to render the Arrangement or chosen range.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has Quick Audio Export and a detailed multi-format Export dialog.
proposed_migration_behavior: Bind Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R to Quick Export by default and expose Advanced Export without changing Ardour's rendering engine.
acceptance_criterion: The shortcut exports the session or selected range to the chosen WAV/FLAC preset with the Master path rendered.
risk_note: Profile templates must define start/end markers and Master routing.

ableton_user_goal: Export individual tracks or buses as stems
live_behavior: Use Export Audio/Video with rendered track options.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour has dedicated Stem Export with optional track/bus processing.
proposed_migration_behavior: Expose Stem Export in the migration command palette and ship unprocessed/processed format presets.
acceptance_criterion: Selected tracks and buses export as synchronized files with the chosen processing policy.
risk_note: MIDI-only interchange requires separate MIDI export guidance.

ableton_user_goal: Commit processing to audio or reduce DSP load
live_behavior: Freeze/Flatten or Bounce to Audio while retaining an editable workflow.
ardour_native_capability: Ardour can bounce regions with or without processing; full track-freeze workflow and recovery semantics differ.
proposed_migration_behavior: Provide Bounce Selection with Processing immediately; treat reversible whole-track freeze as a separate audited capability.
acceptance_criterion: A selected MIDI/audio passage can be rendered through its processors to a new audio region while the original remains recoverable.
risk_note: Do not label destructive or manual bounce steps as exact Freeze/Flatten parity.
